question: What does HTML stand for?
explanation: HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language, the standard markup language for creating web pages.

question: What is the correct declaration to specify HTML5 document standard mode?
explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> is the standard declaration that tells web browsers the document is written in HTML5.

question: Which HTML element is the root element that encloses all other page content?
explanation: The <html> tag is the root container of an HTML document.

question: Inside which HTML element are metadata tags like <title>, <meta>, and <link> placed?
explanation: The <head> section contains machine-readable metadata and links to styles/scripts, not visible in the page body.

question: Which HTML tag is used to define the title of the webpage displayed on the browser tab?
explanation: <title> defines the title that appears in the browser tab and search engine results.

question: Where does the visible content of a web page (headings, text, images, tables) reside?
explanation: The <body> element holds all user-visible document structure and media.

question: How many levels of standard headings are available in HTML?
explanation: HTML provides 6 levels of headings, ranging from <h1> (most prominent) to <h6> (least prominent).

question: Which tag defines the most important, highest-level heading on a web page?
explanation: <h1> represents the top-level main heading on a page.

question: Which tag defines the smallest, least prominent standard heading in HTML?
explanation: <h6> is the lowest level heading in HTML.

question: Which HTML tag is used to create a standard paragraph of text?
explanation:
The

tag is used for paragraphs, automatically adding vertical spacing before and after.

question: Which HTML tag inserts a single line break without starting a new paragraph?
explanation: produces a line break in text (it is a self-closing/empty tag).

question: Which HTML tag inserts a horizontal thematic break or dividing line?
explanation: <hr> inserts a horizontal rule across the page.

question: How do you write a comment in HTML that is ignored by web browsers?
explanation: HTML comments use the syntax <!-- comment text -->.

question: Which tag makes text bold purely for visual presentation?
explanation: <b> renders text bold without conveying any extra semantic importance.

question: Which tag renders text bold AND indicates strong semantic importance for accessibility?
explanation: <strong> indicates that its contents have strong importance, seriousness, or urgency.

question: Which tag renders text in italic font purely for visual styling?
explanation: <i> renders text in italic without extra semantic importance.

question: Which tag renders text in italics to indicate verbal stress emphasis?
explanation: <em> represents stressed emphasis that changes the meaning of a sentence.

question: Which tag underlines text in HTML?
explanation: <u> renders text with an underline.

question: Which tag renders text with a strikethrough (cross-out line through text)?
explanation: <s> and <del> render text struck through.

question: Which tag creates subscript text (like the '2' in H₂O)?
explanation: <sub> creates subscript text rendered below the baseline.

question: Which tag creates superscript text (like the '2' in x²)?
explanation: <sup> creates superscript text rendered above the baseline.

question: Which tag displays preformatted text where spaces and line breaks are preserved exactly as typed?
explanation: <pre> renders text in a fixed-width font and preserves all whitespace and newlines.

question: Which tag displays inline computer code snippets with a monospace font?
explanation: <code> is used to indicate a fragment of computer code.

question: Which tag highlights text with a default yellow background in modern HTML5?
explanation: <mark> marks text as highlighted for reference purposes.

question: Which HTML tag defines a short inline quotation?
explanation: <q> defines an inline quotation, automatically adding quotation marks in most browsers.

question: Which tag is used to create a hyperlink in HTML?
explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag creates hyperlinks connecting to other pages, files, or locations.

question: Which attribute of the <a> tag specifies the destination URL of a link?
explanation: The 'href' (hypertext reference) attribute specifies the destination web address.

question: Which attribute makes a hyperlink open in a new browser tab or window?
explanation: target='_blank' instructs the browser to open the link in a new tab.

question: How do you create an email link that opens the user's default email program?
explanation: mailto:info@example.com creates an email link.

question: How do you link to an element with id='contact' on the same webpage?
explanation: href='#contact' creates an in-page anchor jump to the element with id='contact'.

question: Which tag is used to display an image on a webpage?
explanation: The tag embeds images on web pages (it is an empty/void element).

question: Which attribute specifies the image file path or URL in an tag?
explanation: 'src' (source) points to the file location of the image.

question: Why is the 'alt' attribute mandatory on tags?
options: It provides alternative text if the image fails to load and for screen readers used by visually impaired users
It links the image to Google
explanation: 'alt' text is essential for web accessibility (screen readers) and displays if image loading fails.

question: Which attributes are used to set the width and height of an image in pixels?
explanation: width='300' height='200' set pixel dimensions on images.

question: Which tag creates an UNORDERED (bulleted) list?
explanation: <ul> (unordered list) creates a list with bullet points.

question: Which tag creates an ORDERED (numbered) list?
explanation: <ol> (ordered list) creates a numbered list (1, 2, 3...).

question: Which tag is used to define individual list items inside either <ul> or <ol>?
explanation: <li> (list item) represents individual entries inside lists.

question: Which attribute changes the numbering type of an ordered list (e.g., A, B, C or I, II, III)?
explanation: The 'type' attribute (e.g. type='A', type='I', type='1') specifies numbering style.

question: Which tag creates a description list (glossary of terms and definitions)?
explanation: <dl> creates a description list containing term (<dt>) and description (<dd>) pairs.

question: Which tag defines the term/name in a description list?
explanation: <dt> (description term) defines the concept or name.

question: Which tag defines the explanation/definition of a term in a description list?
explanation: <dd> (description definition) provides the details of the term.

question: Which global attribute assigns a unique identifier to an HTML element (must be unique per page)?
explanation: The 'id' attribute must be unique within an HTML document.

question: Which global attribute allows multiple elements to share the same styling or classification?
explanation: The 'class' attribute groups multiple elements for CSS styling and JS selection.

question: Which attribute provides extra advisory information displayed as a tooltip on hover?
explanation: The global 'title' attribute displays advisory text when hovering over an element.

question: Which attribute specifies inline CSS styles directly on an element?
explanation: style='color: red; font-size: 16px;' applies inline CSS styling.

question: Which attribute sets the human language of an element or document?
explanation: lang='en' or lang='ta' specifies the primary language of the content.

question:
Is HTML tag syntax case-sensitive (e.g., is

the same as

)?
options: No, HTML is case-insensitive, but lowercase is standard best practice
explanation: HTML is case-insensitive, but lowercase is the universal W3C standard best practice.

An element that has no closing tag and cannot contain child content (e.g.

, )
explanation:
Void elements like ,
,
, and do not require closing tags.

question: Which tag is used to connect an external CSS stylesheet into an HTML page?
explanation: <link rel='stylesheet' href='style.css'> links external stylesheets.

question: Which tag is used to write internal CSS directly inside an HTML file?
explanation: The <style> tag embeds CSS rules directly inside the <head> of an HTML document.

question: Which tag defines an HTML table?
explanation: The <table> tag creates a tabular grid of rows and columns.

question: Which tag defines a table row in an HTML table?
explanation: <tr> stands for table row.

question: Which tag defines a standard table data cell?
explanation: <td> stands for table data (cell).

question: Which tag defines a table header cell (with default bold, centered text)?
explanation: <th> stands for table header.

question: Which table attribute merges a cell across 2 or more columns horizontally?
explanation: colspan='2' merges a cell across 2 columns horizontally.

question: Which table attribute merges a cell across 2 or more rows vertically?
explanation: rowspan='2' merges a cell across 2 rows vertically.

question: Which tag adds an optional title or caption to an HTML table?
explanation: <caption> defines a table caption, positioned directly after the <table> opening tag.

question: Which tags group the header, body, and footer of an HTML table?
explanation: <thead>, <tbody>, and <tfoot> semantically group table rows.

question: Which tag creates an interactive HTML form to collect user inputs?
explanation: The <form> element defines an HTML form for collecting user inputs.

question: Which attribute of <form> specifies the destination URL where submitted form data is sent?
explanation: The 'action' attribute specifies the URL where the form data is submitted.

question: Which attribute of <form> specifies the HTTP request method used (GET or POST)?
explanation: The 'method' attribute specifies GET (visible in URL) or POST (sent in HTTP body).

question: Which input type creates a single-line text input field?
explanation: <input type='text'> creates a standard single-line text input field.

question: Which input type masks characters with dots or stars for password entry?
explanation: <input type='password'> obscures entered text for security.

question: Which input type creates a clickable button to send form data to the server?
explanation: <input type='submit'> or <button type='submit'> submits form data.

question: Which input type allows a user to select exactly ONE option from a group of choices?
explanation: <input type='radio'> allows selecting only one option from a group sharing the same 'name'.

question: Which input type allows selecting ZERO, ONE, or MULTIPLE independent choices?
explanation: <input type='checkbox'> lets users select multiple independent options.

question: Which attribute ensures an input field must be filled in before form submission?
explanation: The boolean 'required' attribute prevents form submission if the field is empty.

question: Which attribute displays grey hint text inside an input box before typing begins?
explanation: placeholder='Enter name' provides temporary guide text.

question: Which attribute sets the initial pre-filled value of a text input field?
explanation: value='Hello' sets the initial content of an input element.

question: Which tag is used for multi-line text input (e.g. feedback, comments)?
explanation: <textarea> creates a multi-line input box.

question: Which tag creates a drop-down selection list?
explanation: The <select> element creates a drop-down list.

question: Which tag defines individual selectable choices inside a <select> dropdown?
explanation: <option> elements represent individual choices within a <select> list.

question: Which tag associates a descriptive text label with a form control for better accessibility?
explanation: <label for='email'> links descriptive text to an input field.

question: Which input type allows selecting a date from a calendar picker in HTML5?
explanation: <input type='date'> displays a native calendar date picker.

question: Which input type displays a color palette picker?
explanation: <input type='color'> provides a color picker interface.

question: Which semantic tag represents major website navigation links?
explanation: <nav> wraps navigation links (e.g. Home, About, Contact).

question: Which semantic tag represents introductory content or logo/navigation at the top of a page?
explanation: <header> holds introductory content, branding, or search bars.

question: Which semantic tag represents footer content (copyright, contact, privacy) at the bottom?
explanation: <footer> represents the footer of a document or section.

question: Which semantic tag defines an independent, self-contained article or blog post?
explanation: <article> represents a self-contained composition that makes sense on its own.

question: Which semantic tag groups related thematic content, usually with its own heading?
explanation: <section> groups thematic content together.

question: Which semantic tag represents sidebars or content tangentially related to the main content?
explanation: <aside> represents auxiliary content like sidebars, ads, or author bios.

question: Which semantic tag represents the dominant, primary central content of the page?
explanation: <main> wraps the unique central content of the document.

question: What is the primary difference between a block-level element and an inline element?
options: Block elements always start on a new line and take full width; inline elements only take as much width as necessary
Block elements can only have numbers; inline can have text
explanation:
Block elements (
,

,

) start on a new line; inline elements (, , ) stay on the same line.

question: Which of the following is a generic BLOCK-level container with no special visual styling?
explanation: <div> (division) is the standard generic block-level container.

question: Which of the following is a generic INLINE container used to style parts of text?
explanation: <span> is a generic inline container used to style or script text segments.

question: Which of the following elements is an INLINE element by default?
explanation: <a> (hyperlink) is an inline element.

question: Which of the following elements is a BLOCK element by default?
explanation: <div> is a block-level element.

question: Which tag is used to embed and play audio files natively in HTML5?
explanation: The <audio> element embeds sound files without external plugins.

question: Which attribute adds play, pause, and volume controls to an <audio> or <video> tag?
explanation: The boolean 'controls' attribute adds native playback buttons.

question: Which tag is used to embed and play video clips natively in HTML5?
explanation: The <video> tag embeds video files (MP4, WebM) natively.

question: Which attribute specifies a preview thumbnail image shown before a video starts playing?
explanation: poster='thumbnail.jpg' sets the preview image before video playback.

question: Which tag is used inside <audio> or <video> to provide multiple alternative file formats?
explanation: <source src='...' type='...'> provides fallback formats.

question: Which attribute makes an audio or video file start playing automatically upon page load?
explanation: 'autoplay' instructs the media to start playing as soon as ready.

question: Which attribute makes an audio or video repeat from the beginning when it finishes?
explanation: 'loop' makes media replay automatically.

question: Which tag embeds another independent webpage inside the current webpage?
explanation: <iframe> (inline frame) embeds another document inside the current HTML page.

question: Which HTML5 element provides a drawable bitmap surface scripted with JavaScript?
explanation: <canvas> creates a raster bitmap canvas for JS animation and drawing.

question: Which HTML5 tag is used to draw vector graphics using XML tags (scalable without quality loss)?
explanation: <svg> (Scalable Vector Graphics) renders resolution-independent vector shapes.

question: Which input type restricts user entry strictly to numbers on mobile keyboards?
explanation: <input type='number'> opens a numeric keypad and restricts input to numbers.

question: Which input type provides built-in email address syntax validation?
explanation: <input type='email'> verifies that the value conforms to standard email format.

question: What is the default method attribute of an HTML <form> if not explicitly specified?
explanation: If omitted, the default form submission method is GET.
